name: Metro Brands Ltd
title: Metro Brands Ltd - 543426 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Metro Brands Q4 FY26: standalone revenue up 20%, PAT up 18%, FY26 delivered within guidance (sales +15%, PAT mid-teens) despite slow start.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 standalone growth of 20% with EBITDA up 20% and PAT up 18%, and said FY26 metrics landed in guidance after a slow start to the year. Digital commerce grew 53% and reached 12% of revenue in the quarter. The company ended the quarter with 1,032 stores after a net addition of 42, and opened its first two FILA stores since the acquisition. Management flagged input cost inflation from the Gulf crisis (around 10% on affected items), which it plans to mitigate through forward buying and pre-built inventory of about six months.

financial_highlights.metric: Digital commerce share of total revenue (Q4 FY26)

financial_highlights.change: net addition of 42 in the quarter
Q4 was 14%; management said in line with range of 13-15%

segments.name: Metro Mochi / core network
segments.commentary: Management cited footfall growth and rising bills in Metro stores, with revenue per square foot held at 4,500 sq ft across Q3 to Q4. Management said same-store growth (SSG) is the main driver of growth, not just new stores, and believes it is gaining market share.

segments.name: Digital commerce (e-commerce and omnichannel)
segments.commentary: Grew 53% in Q4 and made up 12% of revenue. Management expects it to stay in a 12% to 15% share of business in the near term, with lumpiness around festive periods.

segments.name: FILA
segments.commentary: Two stores opened since acquisition. Management spent time and money clearing old inventory and is repositioning the brand with local manufacturing, expecting it to be meaningful to numbers in about 18 months.

segments.name: Foot Locker
segments.commentary: Store expansion held back by BIS certification uncertainty; management said it does not yet have full comfort that BIS challenges are mitigated.

segments.name: Clarks
segments.commentary: Has no stores in India currently per management; BIS impact is limited because production has moved to India.

segments.name: Walkway (value segment)
segments.commentary: Expansion elevated in FY26; management said it is still refining the format for Tier-2 to Tier-4 towns and high streets, and that profitability and ROCE of the model are improving.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term guidance of 15% to 18% sales growth was referenced by analysts; management said it is confident of sustaining around 15% growth year on year over the long term but would not commit to 15% every quarter.
Management said there are about 50 store openings available across FILA, Foot Locker, Clarks and MetroActiv in FY27, but realisation depends on locations, rentals and BIS clearance.

Input costs: management quantified inflation at around 10% on affected items; expects gradual impact given about six months of inventory and forward-protected orders, with no immediate price hikes planned beyond normal inflation.
Gulf crisis and geopolitical disruption are being monitored for raw materials and input costs.
capex_capacity: New DC opened in March 2026, adding 200,000 sq ft of storage capacity.
Store POS system upgrade to start in June 2026, targeted for rollout by year-end; SAP upgrade planned later in FY27.
Store rental competition has stabilised rather than reverted; management said it is not back to the earlier environment but acceleration has eased.
Store expansion guided as 'as many good ones as we can find'; company described itself as well capitalised.
demand_pricing: Management said Q4 demand improvement came from marketing initiatives, new product launches and CRM-driven acquisition of new customers, not from any single factor such as festive or wedding timing.
Management expects premium customers to be relatively insulated from inflation; Walkway's value customer is more exposed.
Management said footwear is infrequent and not a high-ticket purchase, limiting demand sensitivity to inflation.
Men's and unisex category shifts were attributed to reclassification by third-party brands; combined mix unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: How much is input cost inflation and will prices rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Nissan Joseph put input cost inflation at around 10% on affected items, mitigated by bulk forward buying and six months of inventory; no knee-jerk price hikes, only normal inflation. Kaushal Parekh said higher inventory reflects front-loading ahead of the price rise.

qa_highlights.question: Is growth driven by SSG or new stores, and what is footfall trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SSG is the main driver along with new stores and annualisation; revenue per sq ft held at 4,500 sq ft; in-store footfall and new customer acquisition improved through the back half of the year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the medium-term growth outlook for FY27 and store pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 50 stores are available across FILA, Foot Locker, Clarks and MetroActiv in FY27, but BIS, rentals and timing remain uncertain; growth of around 15% is targeted long-term, with no quarter-by-quarter commitment.

qa_highlights.question: When will Foot Locker BIS issues and FILA repositioning normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not predict BIS clearance timing; FILA repositioning takes time with inventory clean-up, and management expects it to be meaningful in about 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company out of the hyper-competitive rental market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not out of it, but the acceleration in rental competition has stabilised.

risks_watch: BIS certification uncertainty for Foot Locker and MetroActiv, which depend on imported products; management said it is a constraint on store openings.
Input cost inflation of about 10% on certain categories linked to crude and the Gulf crisis; pricing response is yet to be determined.
FILA turnaround timeline (about 18 months) and cleared inventory costs.
Lumpiness in e-commerce around festive seasons and brand sale timing.
Macro pressure on white-collar consumers, which management acknowledged as a potential risk.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Q4 execution and the store and tech pipeline, but cautious and at times evasive on BIS timing, store-count commitments and quarter-by-quarter growth, which management described as unpredictable.
key_quotes: we are not going to have to see that spike, and because we are so far planned out, we are able to then figure out how best to mitigate it
So, for me to commit and say every single quarter will be at 15% is a little bit erratic on my part.
It's out of my hands to predict.
